title: Several minds in one room
subtitle: A team chat where humans and several model seats work together, each seat answering only when addressed, with no loop an agent can start
technologies: Context engineering and persistent agent memory
Idempotency, exactly-once effects and crash recovery

stats.label: fixed model seats, plus Helix itself
deadline for a prompt to appear in the provider's own transcript

lede: Most AI chat is one person and one model in a private window. My work is a team: several people, several models from different families, documents on the table, and decisions that have to outlive the session. Helix puts all of that in one room on an open-source team chat server. Each model is a named participant with its own identity. A person addresses a seat the way they address a colleague, the seat answers in the right thread under its own name, and the room keeps the history. The chat server runs unmodified from a pinned image, with its bundled calling and AI plugins switched off, so Helix is the only AI and voice authority in the room.
quote: The room is the authority, and no model holds the shared state.
evidence: Multi-agent collaboration systems: people and 8 fixed model seats from 3 model families working in one chat room, each seat answering only when addressed.
Exactly-once delivery and crash recovery: intake and output keyed so a retry repairs a missing post and never runs a model turn twice.
Context engineering for LLM agents: each turn assembled from a bounded set of inputs, older context left in the seat's own session, credentials never in a prompt.
Delivery verification for agent prompts: a prompt counts as delivered only when it appears in the provider's own transcript within 30 s.
author: Corey James
